clue.text: Tiny model whose charges are small

blocks.note: baby as an adjective means very small
an artist's model sits for a portrait, so is a sitter

explanation.surface: A petite fashion model is described as having young dependants.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a cryptic description: the person whose charges are small is minding little children.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone paid to mind infants has young children temporarily in their care, and those children are little.

clue.text: Clog dance

blocks.note: first meaning: to clump together and block
second meaning: a formal social event with dancing

explanation.surface: A clog dance is a traditional dance in wooden shoes.
explanation.walkthrough: Clog dancing is a folk dance in wooden-soled shoes, but here clog is a verb: snow can ball and clog a horse's hooves.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball as a verb means to form into a clump that blocks, and as a noun is a grand formal dancing party.

clue.text: As porter will do in Paddington, say

blocks.note: first meaning: what a porter does with luggage, carry it
second meaning: Paddington is the famous Peruvian children's-book animal found at the London station

explanation.surface: Porters carry bags at Paddington, the London railway terminus.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddington is both a London station and Michael Bond's marmalade-loving storybook character.
explanation.definitionFit: To carry a load is to bear it, and Paddington is a fictional example of the animal.

clue.text: Ram-raider getting away with the stock

definitions.text: Ram-raider getting away with the stock

blocks.clueFragment: Ram-raider getting away with the stock
blocks.note: surface reading: a thief who smashes a car through a shop front to escape with its merchandise
setter's reading: a raider of rams, someone rustling the farmer's livestock

explanation.walkthrough: Ram-raiding is the British crime of driving a vehicle through a shop window to loot it; here the ram is the animal and the stock is livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A rustler who takes woolly farm animals from the flock is a thief of that particular livestock.

clue.text: Italian poet didn't stand up like this

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: someone who didn't stand sat
so means in this way

explanation.surface: An Italian poet refused to rise, sitting in a particular manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Torquato Tasso was the sixteenth-century Italian author of the epic Jerusalem Delivered.

clue.text: With awful noise about, fail to catch broadcasts

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters of the next word are jumbled
about means going round, so the jumbled letters wrap around the other piece

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
to miss a ball is to fail to catch it

explanation.surface: Amid dreadful racket, someone misses hearing the radio programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: Emissions are things sent out, such as signals transmitted by a radio station.

clue.text: Some metal containing mineral

indicators.note: only some of the following run of letters is wanted, a portion lying across two words

blocks.note: the letters straddle the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A mineral is described as containing some metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is a soft magnesium silicate mineral, ground to make talcum powder.

clue.text: Native inhabitant fixing oil bargain

indicators.note: fixing something rearranges or alters it, so the following letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A local resident is arranging a cheap fuel deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An aboriginal is an original or indigenous dweller of a land, present from the earliest times.

clue.text: Conservative's elected leader in suffering after party reversal

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
in places the selected letter inside the following phrase

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative
the morning-after misery following a night of drinking
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Tory politician's newly chosen leader is suffering after the party's political reversal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering after party' reads as the morning-after headache of a drinker, not political misery; the elected leader's initial sits inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A changeover is a switch from one system or side to another, a reversal of arrangements.

clue.text: Editorials written by  trendy bosses

blocks.note: a leader is a newspaper's leading article or editorial
hip means fashionable

explanation.surface: Fashionable executives are penning the newspaper's opinion columns.
explanation.definitionFit: The bosses of an organisation collectively form its top management, the group in charge.

clue.text: Fish with a tailpiece

blocks.note: a common sea fish
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fish is described as having a tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tailpiece' suits the fish picture, but it is the musical sense: a closing passage.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage added at the end of a musical piece or literary work.

clue.text: A shake of the head, maybe - it doesn't add up

definitions.text: A shake of the head, maybe

blocks.clueFragment: A shake of the head, maybe
blocks.note: first meaning: a gesture meaning no
second meaning: the minus symbol, which subtracts rather than adds

explanation.surface: Someone shakes their head because the figures don't make sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A head-shake signals refusal, and the arithmetic minus symbol indicates subtraction rather than addition.

clue.text: Rising composer's going wrong right away, padding out suite, say

indicators.note: right stands for one letter of the word before it, and away tells us to drop that letter

blocks.note: rising means going up
Gustav Holst, composer of The Planets
erring means going astray, doing wrong

explanation.surface: A rising composer is going astray, writing to pad out a musical suite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' simply gives UP here; one R is dropped from ERRING. 'Suite' is a set of furniture, a sofa and armchairs, not music.
explanation.definitionFit: Upholstering is fitting stuffing and covers to furniture such as a three-piece suite of sofa and chairs.

clue.text: It's not just part of a leap year

definitions.text: It's not just part of a leap year

blocks.clueFragment: It's not just part of a leap year
blocks.note: surface reading: something more than a portion of a year with 29 days in February
setter's reading: a leap is a jump, and the season named after a jump is a part of any year

explanation.walkthrough: The season's name is also a word for a leap, so it is literally part of a leap year, yet it comes round in every year, not just those.
explanation.definitionFit: The season between winter and summer is one quarter of every calendar year.

clue.text: Policeman's given cover to hold unruly lout

indicators.note: unruly means disorderly, so the letters of the next word are jumbled
to give cover is to wrap around, so the policeman encloses what follows

blocks.note: copper is slang for a police officer
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A police officer is called in to restrain a disorderly yob.
explanation.definitionFit: A clodhopper is a clumsy, boorish oaf, the sort of uncouth bumpkin called a lout.

clue.text: Communist leaders built poor revolution

indicators.note: a revolution overturns the existing order, so the preceding letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Communist rulers made a mess of building a revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: The Politburo was the chief policy-making committee of the Soviet Communist Party, its ruling inner circle.

clue.text: Where the wax often goes it protects bodywork

blocks.note: first meaning: sealing wax sits beneath the stamped seal on a document
second meaning: an anti-rust coating applied to a car's underside

explanation.surface: Car wax is applied to protect a vehicle's paintwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Underseal is a British term for the bitumen-like coating sprayed under a car against rust.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it locates the wax below the seal; as one word it is a rustproofing coating for vehicles.

clue.text: I run after a male friend

indicators.note: after says the first-named pair of pieces is placed behind the pair that follows it in the clue

blocks.note: taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for male
taken as written
to go is to run, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Someone jogs behind a man who is their pal.
explanation.definitionFit: Amigo is the Spanish word for a pal, borrowed into casual English speech.

clue.text: Country backing assistance to Ulster

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the following words are read from right to left

blocks.note: aid is help
Northern Ireland, often called Ulster, abbreviated NI

explanation.surface: A country is supporting aid to Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulster is the historic province that roughly makes up Northern Ireland, abbreviated NI.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation of South Asia, fitting the plain geographical clue.

clue.text: To indulge in pleasure, one's needing little drink in amorous encounter

indicators.note: the amorous encounter needs these letters placed inside it to be complete

blocks.note: a romantic date
one is I, plus the 's
a sip is a small mouthful

explanation.surface: Someone seeking pleasure has a small drink on a romantic evening out.
explanation.walkthrough: The old intransitive sense of the verb, to live a dissolute life, is what the definition points to; 'one's' supplies the I plus the S of the apostrophe.
explanation.definitionFit: To dissipate, intransitively, once meant living a dissolute life of pleasure-seeking and self-indulgence.

clue.text: One widely travelled theatre-goer?

blocks.note: first meaning: a person who has toured all over the world
second meaning, whimsical: someone who keeps trotting off to Shakespeare's reconstructed playhouse in London

explanation.walkthrough: The Globe is Shakespeare's theatre on London's South Bank; a regular there trots off to it, while the world-traveller trots around the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who travels all over the world is called this, literally one trotting across the planet.

clue.text: Rapid beating spoiled broth

indicators.note: something spoiled is ruined, so the next word's letters are messed up

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Too many cooks, perhaps: the soup has been ruined by fast whisking.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is a strong pulsing rhythm, like a heart pounding fast with emotion.

clue.text: Eager for compromise between giants?

indicators.note: a compromise meets halfway, so one name gives up a letter to come closer to the other

blocks.note: Gog and Magog are the legendary giants of London's Guildhall; the longer name is used

explanation.surface: Someone is keen for the two giants to strike a deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Gog and Magog are a pair of legendary giants; a word halfway between the two names drops the M from MAGOG.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means keenly excited and impatient to see or hear something, wide-eyed with eagerness.

clue.text: Oarsmen reportedly land in midstream

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word is judged by how it sounds

blocks.note: a rowing eight is a crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Rowers are said to land on a river island.
explanation.walkthrough: An eight is a racing boat with eight rowers; eyot is pronounced like eight.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyot, or ait, is a small island in a river, especially on the Thames.

clue.text: Agent's admission it's just a game

blocks.note: first meaning: a secret agent owning up to being one
second meaning: the children's guessing game played with letters

explanation.surface: A spy confesses but insists it is all only play.
explanation.walkthrough: The children's game begins 'I spy with my little eye something beginning with...'.
explanation.definitionFit: A confessing secret operative would say these words, which also name a children's guessing pastime.

clue.text: Yens to hold distraught grannie left with great longing

indicators.note: someone distraught is all over the place, so the following letters are jumbled
to hold is to have inside, so the yens wrap around what follows

blocks.note: Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese currency, so two of them give two Ys
the letters to be rearranged
L is the standard abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Granny, abandoned and upset, has strong cravings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yens' looks like cravings, which suits the surface, but here it means two yen, each abbreviated Y; they enclose the rearranged GRANNIE plus L.
explanation.definitionFit: Yearningly is the adverb describing doing something while wanting it intensely and wistfully.

clue.text: Attention given to Liberal peer

blocks.note: to give someone your ear is to pay attention
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician is listened to by a member of the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above viscount, so a member of the peerage.

clue.text: Bad debtor has flutter when in the black

blocks.note: to flutter is to fly with flapping wings
in the black of darkness is by night

explanation.surface: A debtor who can't pay is having a bet while still in credit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flutter' is British slang for a small bet and 'in the black' means in credit, both suiting a debtor; here they mean flying and darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: A fly-by-night is an unreliable person who slips away at night to avoid paying what they owe.
